item.title: Will Smith Defeats Sexual Harassment Lawsuit Brought by ‘America’s Got Talent’ Violinist
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to our latest update on the world of entertainment. Today, we're talking about a significant development in a lawsuit involving Will Smith.
[Music transitions to a neutral background tone]
Host: An electric violinist, Brian King Joseph, who performed on Will Smith's Based on a True Story tour, had filed a lawsuit against the actor and rapper, alleging sexual harassment. But in a recent court order, the judge has thrown out the lawsuit.
[Pause for emphasis]
Host: According to the court documents, Joseph claimed he was fired after reporting a break-in at his hotel room during a Las Vegas stop, where he found sexually suggestive materials and a note that read, "Brian, I'll be back." However, the judge found that while the note was sexual in nature, it didn't rise to the level of workplace sexual misconduct.
[Neutral tone continues]
Host: The judge also stated that Joseph had no evidence to suggest that Smith or his staff were responsible for the alleged break-in, which they deny happened. As a result, the judge dismissed not only the sexual harassment claims but also Joseph's allegations of wrongful termination and retaliation.
[Music transitions to a wrap-up tone]
Host: Although the lawsuit has been dismissed, Joseph is allowed to rework and refile his case if he chooses to do so. We'll be keeping an eye on this story for any further developments. That's all for now. Thanks for tuning in.
[Outro music plays]
